This file checks the data before we commit to it and runs the two steps of our
main analysis on a first pass. Run `R/01_get_data.R` first.

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(tidyverse)

tracks <- read_csv(here::here("data", "spotify_tracks_clean.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
```

## 1. Size and missing values

```{r}
#| label: size
nrow(tracks)
n_distinct(tracks$track_genre)

tracks |>
  summarise(across(everything(), \(x) sum(is.na(x)))) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "variable", values_to = "n_missing") |>
  filter(n_missing > 0)
```

## 2. Outcome (popularity) and explanatory variable (danceability)

```{r}
#| label: summaries
tracks |>
  summarise(mean_pop = mean(popularity), sd_pop = sd(popularity),
            share_zero_pop = mean(popularity == 0),
            mean_dance = mean(danceability), sd_dance = sd(danceability))

ggplot(tracks, aes(popularity)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 2) +
  labs(x = "Spotify popularity (0-100)", y = "Number of tracks")

ggplot(tracks, aes(danceability)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.02) +
  labs(x = "Danceability (0-1)", y = "Number of tracks")
```

## 3. Step 1: overall relationship (H1)

```{r}
#| label: step1
cor(tracks$danceability, tracks$popularity)

ggplot(tracks, aes(danceability, popularity)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.03) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
  labs(x = "Danceability", y = "Spotify popularity")

# Mean popularity by danceability group
tracks |>
  mutate(dance_group = cut(danceability, breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.2), include.lowest = TRUE)) |>
  group_by(dance_group) |>
  summarise(n = n(), mean_pop = mean(popularity))

m1 <- lm(popularity ~ danceability, data = tracks)
summary(m1)
```

## 4. Step 2: within genre (H2)

```{r}
#| label: step2
m2 <- lm(popularity ~ danceability + track_genre, data = tracks)

# Compare the danceability slope with and without genre
tibble(
  model = c("popularity ~ danceability", "popularity ~ danceability + track_genre"),
  danceability_slope = c(coef(m1)["danceability"], coef(m2)["danceability"])
)

# Relationship in the six genres with the most tracks
top_genres <- tracks |> count(track_genre, sort = TRUE) |> slice_head(n = 6) |> pull(track_genre)

tracks |>
  filter(track_genre %in% top_genres) |>
  ggplot(aes(danceability, popularity)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.1) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
  facet_wrap(~ track_genre) +
  labs(x = "Danceability", y = "Spotify popularity")
```
